rule: decision 47: a mapping the blind verifier did not confirm is held — never shown, never a diagnosis, never S5 evidence — until a human keeps or drops it

items.stem: Solve $x^3 + 6x^2 + 11x + 6 = 0$. Tap every solution on the number line.
items.construction: x^3+6x^2+11x+6=(x+1)(x+2)(x+3), so the roots are -1, -2, -3. Tap -3, -2 and -1 on the number line (range [-6,6]). All are whole numbers inside the range and there are 3 targets, within the 1–4 limit.
items.predicate_meaning: Marked values that the answer set does not contain
items.hint: Substitute each marked value into $P(x)$; only values giving $0$ are solutions.
items.why: It can fire, e.g. when the student marks 1 or -4. The hint is mathematically right. But the question never defines P(x), so the notation is unclear to the student. When in doubt, false.

items.stem: Solve $x^4-5x^2+4=0$. Tap every solution on the number line.
items.construction: Factor as (x^2-1)(x^2-4)=0, so x^2=1 or x^2=4, giving x=±1 and ±2. Mark -2, -1, 1, 2 on the range [-6,6]. That is 4 whole-number targets inside the range, so it is reachable.
items.predicate_meaning: Right sizes, wrong signs — a value marked as its negative, as when (x − a) = 0 is read as x = −a
items.hint: Taking the square root gives both signs, so check each value has its partner.
items.why: The answer set {-2,-1,1,2} is symmetric, so the negative of any target is also a target. Flipping signs can never produce a wrong mark, so the predicate never fires meaningfully here. The hint's 'check each value has its partner' also nearly reveals the ± structure.

items.stem: Solve $x^3 - 2x^2 - 5x + 6 = 0$. Tap every solution on the number line.
items.construction: x^3-2x^2-5x+6 factors as (x-1)(x-3)(x+2); roots -2, 1, 3. Tap -2, 1 and 3 on the number line (range [-6,6], all whole numbers inside range, 3 targets).
items.predicate_meaning: Marked values that the answer set does not contain
items.hint: Substitute each marked value into $P(x)$; only values that give $0$ are solutions.
items.why: Fires if the student marks e.g. -2, 1, 3 and also 2. Substituting is valid, but the hint refers to $P(x)$, which the question never defines, so it may confuse the student. Not clearly helpful as written.
